To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) MR and GR are complementary mediators of glucocorticoid action, and (2) MR and GR mediate complementary effects of cortisol in brain circuits underlying stress adaptation and recovery.
“MR and GR mediate the action of cortisol/corticosterone on the onset and termination, respectively, of the CRF/Unc system-driven stress response”.
the CRF/UCN and GR/MR systems interact in a complex and dynamic manner in brain circuits that regulate the stress response and its termination.
In summary, our research is concerned with

understanding the molecular and cellular basis of the stress response and its modulation by glucocorticoids, with the ultimate goal to develop novel therapeutic approaches to stress-related disorders such as depression and anxiety.
the question of how the brain manages to maintain homeostatic balance in response to the challenges of stress, and how genetic and environmental factors influence this process.

the brain-adrenal axis, a system that evolved in the course of evolution to maintain the balance between the organism and its environment, and that is subjected to intrinsic feedback regulation by glucocorticoid hormones.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Wylie Vale legacy is to have opened the door to the study of stress and health from a brain-adrenocortical perspective.
the brain-adrenal axis operates as a self-regulatory feedback loop in which the CRF/Ucns and glucocorticoids interact to maintain a balance between susceptibility to stress and recovery.
Wylie Vale has been a key player in the development of a new and more integrative view on stress and its regulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a balanced CRF/Ucn:glucocorticoids system is essential for the maintenance of health.
the balance between the CRF and Ucn systems is modulated by the MR and GR signaling, which in turn can be modulated by environmental and genetic factors, as well as by experience-related factors.
the CRF/Ucns and glucocorticoids are not only the main orchestrators of the stress response but also its main regulators.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CRF/Unc and glucocorticoids act in complementary fashion on the same brain circuits to orchestrate the stress response and its termination.
the glucocorticoids have an essential function in the maintenance of a balanced stress response, and that this balance is essential for health.
a balanced MR: GR signaling is essential to maintain the integrity of the CRF–Ucn–GR system.
